quickVerdict: Help Scout is the better default for most support teams: it's cheaper per seat at every tier, its AI pricing is cleaner ($0.75/resolution with a published definition versus LiveChat's more fragmented AI story), and its shared-inbox design is what most small-to-mid teams actually need. LiveChat is the better pick specifically if live, real-time website chat is your primary channel and you want the most polished agent experience and integration ecosystem available at any price — it's built for chat-as-a-sales-channel as much as chat-as-support. Most teams choosing between an email-first inbox and a live-chat-first console already know which describes their actual support volume; that answer should decide this comparison before price does.
tldr: Help Scout is an email-first shared inbox that deliberately avoids looking like a ticketing system; LiveChat is a live-chat agent app built for real-time website conversation, with two decades of polish behind the human side of the product.

Both charge per seat, but Help Scout is cheaper at every comparable tier: $25/$45/$75 per user versus LiveChat's $49/$79 for its realistic tiers (Starter is capped at one user), plus LiveChat has no free plan at all against Help Scout's usable free tier.

AI pricing is where Help Scout is meaningfully cleaner: $0.75 per resolution with a published definition of what counts, versus LiveChat's AI Agent being gated to separate 'Text plans' rather than included in a LiveChat subscription, with resolution allowances and packs that are harder to reason about from the pricing page alone.

LiveChat pulls well ahead on integration polish — first-party, no-code apps for WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, and Webflow, plus a genuine public developer platform — where several of Help Scout's website-builder 'integrations' are just documented copy-paste embed instructions.

Help Scout's shared inbox and internal collaboration tools (notes, assignment, AI-powered summaries) are more mature for a distributed team than LiveChat's chat-centric console, which lacks documented internal notes or @mentions.

Pick LiveChat if real-time chat is your primary channel and you want the best-built agent experience money can buy. Pick Help Scout if your support is mostly email/async and you want a cheaper, simpler inbox with cleaner AI economics.

verdict: These two get compared because they're both mature, well-reviewed per-seat platforms, but they're built for genuinely different support shapes. Help Scout's entire design premise is that a customer should never see a ticket number — email, Beacon chat, and connected social channels land in one thread per customer, and reviewers consistently name that intuitiveness as the top strength with near-total consistency. LiveChat's design premise is the opposite: real-time conversation is the product, and two decades of iteration show in genuinely excellent chat mechanics — message sneak-peek, canned responses, chat supervision — backed by a strong, large independent review base. Price tells you which one assumes your support volume. Help Scout is cheaper at every real tier ($25 vs. effectively $49 once you need more than one LiveChat seat), and its AI pricing is the cleaner of the two: $0.75 per resolution with a published definition of what counts, versus LiveChat's autonomous AI Agent living on a separate 'Text plan' structure that isn't even part of the core LiveChat subscription you'd sign up for. Where LiveChat clearly wins is polish outside the core product: first-party, no-code integrations for WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, and Webflow, plus a genuine public developer platform, against Help Scout's website-builder 'integrations' that are mostly documented copy-paste embed code. Both AI stories deserve skepticism — Help Scout's resolution definition rewards an abandoned chat as a success, and LiveChat's 74% figure has no independent corroboration either. My honest take: if live, real-time chat is genuinely your primary support channel and you want the most capable agent experience and integration ecosystem regardless of cost, LiveChat earns its premium. If your support is mostly email and asynchronous conversation and you want a cheaper, simpler inbox with AI pricing you can actually reason about, Help Scout is the more defensible default.
